title: NYC Budget Blueprint
plain_title: Nine budget and management steps proposed for the new mayor
what_they_audited: A Citizens Budget Commission report setting out nine proposals for the incoming Mamdani administration's first New York City budget.
background: The incoming mayor must close a $6 billion to $8 billion budget gap and prepare for federal aid cuts one month into his term.

findings.plain: The city's own projections understate what it expects to spend in fiscal year 2027.
findings.quote: the City’s projections understate fiscal year 2027 spending by $4.5 billion by CBC’s estimate

findings.plain: Over three fiscal years the city spent more than it took in, drawing on money saved during the pandemic-era revenue surge.
findings.quote: Over the past three fiscal years, the City spent $2.3 billion more than it took in

findings.plain: The Rainy Day Fund holds far less than the report estimates would be needed to cover two years of recession-driven revenue declines.
findings.quote: It would need $14.0 billion to cover two years of tax revenue declines, but its Rainy Day Fund only has $2.0 billion.

findings.plain: Few New Yorkers rate city spending or city services well in the group's resident survey.
findings.quote: only 11 percent of New Yorkers believe the City spends their tax dollars wisely and just 27 percent say services are good or excellent

findings.plain: Federal policy changes already enacted will cut aid to the city and reduce support that high-need New Yorkers receive directly.
findings.quote: Dramatic federal policy and budget changes already enacted will reduce aid to the City and cut support high-need New Yorkers receive directly.

recommendations: Work with the Office of Management and Budget to identify the city's total spending obligations, available revenue and risks, and present accurate estimates.
Identify the impact and cost-effectiveness of each service, keep what works well and cut or shrink what does not.
Launch a citywide performance management system modeled on CompStat to drive service quality and budget decisions.
Run a savings plan that streamlines operations, reduces duplication, phases out lower-impact programs, automates manual processes and raises productivity in collaboration with labor unions.
Allocate vacant positions flexibly across agencies rather than agency by agency, eliminate excess vacancies and let agencies hire quickly.
Prepare for federal cuts by realigning city funds toward affordability and the neediest New Yorkers and adding $1 billion a year to the general reserve.

Add to the Rainy Day Fund while revenues are strong and work with the City Council to pass a law setting the fund's target size, requiring deposits during expansions and limiting withdrawals to recessions and emergencies.
Use collective bargaining to turn efficiency gains into funding for wage increases.
